items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I think that’s why he called it “Jazz Messengers” because there was a message there... I know I was criticized for having three black guys in my group for a long time

ctx.x: Can you describe Blakey’s approach and how he drove the band?

[sigh] Well he got, he was one of the few players in history that got stronger as the night went on. Most of the guys would kind of simmer down and flake out and get, not him, he would get more intense and stronger. And he had an inherent feeling that seemed to generate through the band and everybody got it, everybody got that message and I think that’s why he called it “Jazz Messengers” because there was a message there. He was a, the funniest thing, he became a Muslim, he called himself Abdullah Buhaina, and he…
